data.description: is_hard_capacity_stop() matched 'usage limit reached' but not 'hit your usage limit' -- the actual Codex message. One-word regex gap let 1,366 rounds over ~13 hours retry against a provider that had already stated its recovery date (Aug 18). Rule widened to match stable phrases regardless of verb; stop path now records the provider's stated retry time.

Session-rollover request was handled by the manager side-car polling codex_turn_active() externally -- a race it can only win if it happens to poll during a between-turn gap that collapses to sub-second during productive runs (turns 106-134 ran unbroken on one thread despite a pending rollover request, 579M tokens). Moved the check synchronously into the executor's own round loop, at the only point it deterministically knows no turn is active.

RESOLVED, not a metering bug: inspected real per-turn input_tokens for successive turns in the same resumed session (turns 151-155, round 52-56): 172.86M -> 174.14M -> 175.39M -> 177.19M -> 183.36M, steadily growing turn over turn. This is a resumed session (codex exec resume) re-sending its entire accumulated conversation as input context every turn, so input_tokens is a real cumulative total, not a double-counted or fabricated figure -- summing across turns correctly reflects real billed cost across a session's lifetime, however wasteful. The ~4.24B sum across 1444 turns is therefore plausible and real, and is the same mechanism already fixed tonight (session-rollover race, learning_ledger id=2): every turn the rollover failed to fire, the session kept re-billing its whole growing history.
